How gophers damage your property

Don't let underground activity destroy your landscape

Pocket gophers spend much of their lives underground, creating extensive tunnel systems while feeding on roots, bulbs, plants and other vegetation.

The damage shows up as raised soil and unsightly mounds, dying vegetation, severed roots and broken irrigation — and it keeps recurring while the gophers remain underground.

  • Fresh mounds — crescent- or fan-shaped soil mounds appearing again and again
  • Wilting or dying plants — roots severed or damaged underground
  • Damaged irrigation — tunnels interfering with irrigation components
  • Uneven, unstable soil — from extensive underground tunneling
